brief: Market Ear roundup of five desk notes on cross-asset extremes. GS: Mag 7 implied vol is cheap versus broader tech, relative vol ratio at the 15th percentile over four years, even as the NDX/SPX vol spread, down sharply after last week's blowout, still sits at the 94th percentile, so Mag 7 is cheap to tech while tech stays expensive to the broader market. Nomura's McElligott: hedge fund Mag 7 beta is near the 97th percentile historically while mutual fund beta sits near the 11th, a crowded-hedge-fund-versus-underexposed-long-only split. Goldman Prime Brokerage: long/short momentum exposure collapsed from near 70% at the peak to around 15%. JPM's October 20 note: KOSPI trades at 8.4x forward earnings ex-memory giants, an 11th-percentile reading, with RSI at its lowest since Liberation Day, which JPM calls an increasingly attractive setup, even as GS data show Korea net and gross fund allocation have fallen to multi-year lows. TS Lombard: homebuilder margins have fallen below pre-Covid levels on rising costs and soft new-home prices. 7.3% mortgage rates and weak affordability could worsen if the Fed turns more hawkish. Brazil's debt-to-GDP, now 81.9% versus 71.7% in 2023, could reach near 118% by 2036 without reform, risking a shutdown by 2028.
